title: Tool Contract Sentinel and Streaming Ergonomics Kit
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: SDK users across Python/TypeScript/Go are struggling with three recurring issues when integrating tool/function calling into production LLM flows: 1) mismatches between declared function schemas and runtime payloads causing noisy errors and silent failures; 2) awkward streaming ergonomics for long-running tool outputs (developers resort to ad-hoc polling or re-requesting from the API); 3) inconsistent retry semantics across SDKs for transient invocation failures and partial-stream resumptions.

Goal: Deliver a lightweight, cross-language helpers pack that provides (a) runtime validation and coercion for function schemas, (b) an ergonomic streaming iterator with resumable checkpoints and idempotency tokens, and (c) a consistent retry/backoff policy that can be tuned per-language but shares behavior and observability signals. This ticket covers API surface, runtime guards, test harness, and language examples (Python/TS/Go).
technical_design:
Overview: Implement a 'sentinel' layer in each SDK that sits between the SDK user call and the network sender. Responsibilities: (1) pre-invoke validation: compile JSON schema (from model-provided function spec or user-supplied contract) into a runtime validator; provide strict and permissive modes and a 'coerce' option to coerce simple types (numbers-as-strings). (2) invocation wrapper: attach idempotency token, structured metadata for tracing, and transform streaming frames into an async iterator that yields typed 'chunks' plus checkpoint tokens. (3) resume semantics: on transient network failure, use last checkpoint token to request a resume token from the server or replay an idempotent unary call to advance the cursor. (4) retries: implement per-language RetryPolicy with exponential backoff, jitter, and a max-attempts/total-time guard; ensure retries do not re-execute non-idempotent tools without explicit user opt-in.

APIs sketches:
- Python: ToolInvocation.from_schema(schema: str|dict, mode: "strict"|"permissive" = "strict", coerce: bool=False) -> ToolInvoker; invoker.invoke_stream(args, on_chunk=None) -> AsyncIterator[ToolChunk].
- TypeScript: createToolInvoker(schema: JSONSchema, opts?: {mode: 'strict'|'permissive', coerce?: boolean}) -> ToolInvoker; invoker.stream(args): AsyncIterable<ToolChunk>.
- Go: NewToolInvoker(schema []byte, opts ...InvokerOption) -> *ToolInvoker; invoker.Stream(ctx, args) -> <-chan ToolChunk, error channel and checkpoint API.

Validation runtime: use language-appropriate JSON Schema compilers (fastjsonschema in Python, ajv in TS, gojsonschema in Go). Provide a small shim that translates LLM 'function' shapes (parameter lists with descriptions) into canonical JSON Schema to avoid duplicating model-side heuristics. Expose diagnostics for mismatches with Severity: warning|error.

Streaming ergonomics: the iterator yields {chunk_id, payload, progress, checkpoint_token, final:boolean}. Checkpoint tokens encoded as compact base64 JSON with sequence_id and KV hints. Provide example helper to persist checkpoint tokens to local storage and resume with them.

Observability: emit metrics (invocation_attempts, validation_failures, resume_success, stream_bytes, avg_chunk_latency) via SDK telemetry hooks. Attach breadcrumbs to log lines with short hash of schema and invocation id.

Compatibility & safety: default behavior is conservative: strict validation, no automatic retries for non-idempotent tool types (method annotated in schema: "side_effects": true). Provide escape hatches for advanced users (force_retry_non_idempotent: opt-in flag).
acceptance_criteria: Provide working runtime validator codepaths in Python, TS, and Go that accept a JSON Schema and validate sample tool payloads with >95% coverage of common constraints (required, types, enums, nested objects)
Implement streaming iterator that emits checkpoint tokens and supports resuming a stream with persisted checkpoint; demonstrated with integration test against test harness server
RetryPolicy implementation exists in all three SDKs with consistent semantics and unit tests proving backoff/jitter and honor of max-attempts and total-time limits
Documentation pages and one end-to-end example per language (hello_tool) showing: schema registration, invocation, stream consumption, checkpoint persist/resume, and metrics emitted
Performance: pre-invoke validation latency adds <1ms median overhead for small schemas and <10ms 95th percentile for large schemas; measured in microbench harness
Security: security_review_required flagged and review completed for the part of the shim that persists checkpoint tokens (they may contain invocation metadata)
Rollout plan and deprecation notes for existing ad-hoc helpers; migration guide for existing users
tasks: Design document and API review (this ticket)
Prototype validator shim in Python and benchmark compilation time
Implement TS SDK helpers using AJV and publish example package in monorepo/examples
Implement Go streaming channel variant with checkpoint persistence helper
End-to-end integration test harness (server-side resume test) and flaky-test hardening
Telemetry instrumentation and dashboard stub for stream-invoke metrics
Security review for checkpoint storage and idempotency token handling
Cross-SDK consistency pass and public changelog entry
comments: 2025-02-20 - Aisha Patel: Drafted initial design; flagged persistence surface for security review. Linked to design notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SDK/Tool+Sentinel+Design

2025-02-22 - Lina Moreno (Reviews): Suggest exposing both schema 'diagnostics' and 'coercion' results separately so callers can decide whether to record warnings. Also: call out enum coercion behavior in the doc.

2025-02-27 - Liam Chen: Prototype Python validator using fastjsonschema completed. Compiles 95% of test schemas under 0.8ms median. Pushed branch feature/sdk/sentinel-python; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/3921

2025-03-01 - Security team (David Ortiz): Checkpoint tokens must avoid embedding PII. Recommend stamping tokens with invocation-id and pointer to server-side blob; avoid raw args. Marked security_review_required=true.

2025-03-03 - QA (Priya Rao): Integration harness failing intermittently when forcing resume after simulated network partition. Repro linked in test run: https://buildkite.com/redwood/sdk-tests/builds/7742
2025-03-05 - Liam Chen: Added backoff/jitter helper and deterministic time source for tests. Updated tests to use local mock server to remove flakiness. Next: TS implementation and docs.
2025-03-05 - PM (Evan Brooks): Please add migration snippet for existing users who used ad-hoc 'stream_resume' call; we should provide a one-line wrapper to preserve behavior.
